messages:
Ella (PM): quick intake - problem, goals, non-goals, and ask for a short RFC. problem: some enterprise customers are hitting tail latencies and cost spikes when responses go very long (multi-paragraph). clients want a server-side option to "progressively trim" or compress responses to meet latency SLOs while preserving user intent and critical entities (e.g., names, dates, financial amounts). we need a spec for a trimming policy that is configurable per-tenant/route and safe (no silent data loss).

Goals:
- Provide a server-side trimming policy that reduces median and p95 response time for long outputs without retraining models.
- Preserve named entities and required structured fields with configurable strictness.
- Support streaming (so clients can still render progressive output).
- Allow tenants to opt into: soft-trim (summarize/abbreviate) or hard-trim (truncate) and choose a fidelity profile.
- Instrumentation + evals to detect regressions (entity-preservation >= threshold).

Non-goals:
- Not a model training or fine-tuning project; we won't build new models.
- Not client-side SDK changes to mandate behavior (client opt-out must be possible).
- Not replacing per-route QoS/routing policies (this layers on top).

Success metrics (initial):
- P95 generation latency reduced by >= 20% for trimmed requests (per-tenant experiment).
- Cost per long-response request reduced by >= 15% (token billed consumption).
- Entity-preservation F1 >= 0.95 against curated prompt sets for 'strict' mode; >= 0.85 for 'balanced' mode.
- <1% of requests flagged by downstream heuristics as 'incorrectly trimmed' in canary.

Ask: feedback on feasibility, edge cases, rollout guardrails, and suggested acceptance criteria. please call out SRE, privacy, and eval needs. i can draft an RFC after this sync and include a sample config.

Sam (Eng): love the idea. two immediate questions: how does trimming interact with KV cache/prefix caching? if we compress output, do we still cache full output or compressed version? streaming implications too.

Jin (ML Infra): for evals we'll need prompt-level reference outputs and entity-labeling. suggest a 3-way eval: full-output baseline, trimmed output, and a distilled-summary baseline. we can compute entity recall/precision automatically, plus a small human review pool. also: progressive trimming could be implemented as post-processing or via constrained decoding; post-processing is faster to ship.

Olga (SRE): flagging production concerns: trimming changes token output volume unpredictably; we need to check token accounting (billing vs. perceived client tokens), and abort/backpressure semantics for streaming - if we cut earlier, do we close the stream or send a final 'truncated' marker? need explicit fallback policies to avoid half-sent JSON objects.

Amy (Privacy): privacy check: if we remove or omit parts of responses, audit trails must show original prompts and trimming decisions. for regulated tenants we may need to persist both full and trimmed outputs (or at least a hash) for compliance. also call out PII detection: trimming must not drop redaction-required fields.

Miguel (Design): UX idea: expose a small header/metadata in the response that indicates trimming was applied and why (mode, tokens_saved). client can then surface "shortened for latency" with a reveal option. also show diff/highlight of removed sentences when user expands.

Ravi (Data): instrumentation notes: we should log 'trim_reason', 'mode', 'tokens_before', 'tokens_after', 'entities_preserved_count', and correlate with customer SLA alerts. propose an A/B for 10% traffic per-tenant first. acceptance gates: automated entity F1 checks + human review on first 1k trimmed requests.

Sam (Eng): implementation sketch: start as post-processing service in front of the router (layered transformer). config example: 
```
trimming_policy:
  mode: progressive # progressive | hard_truncate | summarize
  budget_tokens: 64  # target token budget for tail trimming
  preserve_entities: true
  entity_whitelist: ["PERSON","DATE","AMOUNT"]
  fallback: fallback_to_truncate # or call_smaller_model
  stream_behavior: send_marker_then_close # or send_marker+summary
```
We'll prototype as opt-in flag on the route.

Olga (SRE): +1 on marker. ensure markers are machine-parseable (e.g., JSON meta chunk). don't let trimming create invalid JSON or break function-calling hooks. add an acceptance test that runs through function-calling routes.

Amy (Privacy): also require an admin-level tenant setting that forces "no trimming" for compliance-bound customers.

Ella (PM): great feedback. next steps i propose: 1) eng drafts a short RFC with implementation approach and rollout plan, 2) ml infra defines eval harness and sample prompts, 3) sre defines streaming/backpressure acceptance tests, 4) privacy defines audit data retention and opt-out controls, 5) design mocks for client metadata/UX. i'll collect these into an RFC template.

Miguel (Design): i can mock the small client header and expanded-diff UX by EOD tomorrow.

Jin (ML Infra): i'll prepare an eval set and a scoring notebook. need PM to surface any tenant-specific edge-case prompts.

Ravi (Data): i'll wire up logging fields to our observability pipeline and propose dashboard widgets for tokens_saved and entity-F1.

Sam (Eng): i'll spin up a prototype branch for post-processing service. low-risk if opt-in. will link RFC draft in a couple days.

OpsBot: created RFC #PRD-4532 and ticket infra: trimmed-output-prototype. assignee: Sam.

Ella (PM): thanks all — can folks drop any must-have acceptance criteria in the RFC thread? i'll schedule a 30-min sync after RFC lands. :thumbsup:
